subject: Custom reliability annex: proposed order-form execution & SOW attachment plan
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@pioneerlabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@pioneerlabs.com, Michael Torres <mtorres@pioneerlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reliability annex request + SOW attachments for order form

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Pioneer Labs is excited about Redwood for inference at scale. Our procurement and engineering teams reviewed the standard MSA/SOW and have two asks before we can sign:

1) A short annex with a small set of tailored availability and latency commitments for our production traffic (we want a 99.95% monthly availability commitment for the inference API with a documented credit schedule).
2) A SOW attachment that calls out the telemetry evidence package and the on-call escalation path for regional failovers. Procurement has asked for explicit language they can put in the order form so legal has a clean path to execution.

Can you send a proposed annex + suggested order-form language and a checklist of the evidence items you’ll deliver (metrics, retention windows, sample runbook pages)? It would help if we could get a version we can circulate to our legal by EOD Thursday (Jun 22).

Also, quick question on exceptions: we have a planned monthly batch job that will generate a burst of long-context requests (up to 8k tokens). We need a documented carve-out so the SLA doesn’t penalize you for that predictable spike. If you can call out a latency/availability exception for scheduled bulk jobs (with a required notification window) that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — Olivia

--
Olivia Grant
Head of Platform Engineering | Pioneer Labs
olivia@pioneerlabs.com
+1 415-555-0187
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@pioneerlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability annex request + SOW attachments for order form

Hi Olivia — great to hear and thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a first-pass annex and SOW attachment that follows the structure you suggested. High-level notes here so procurement/legal have context:

- Availability: proposing a 99.95% monthly availability target for the Hosted inference endpoint in the order form. We define availability as successful API responses (2xx/3xx) within the configured routing region, excluding scheduled maintenance windows.

- Latency commitment: we can include a 95th-percentile response latency target of 300ms for small-context inference (<=512 tokens). For long-context/batched jobs (e.g., your 8k token monthly run), we recommend a carve-out: scheduled bulk jobs will be excluded from SLA calculations if Redwood receives a 48-hour advance notification and the job is marked in the request as "scheduled-bulk".

- Credit schedule: suggested credits tiered by monthly availability: 99.95–100% = no credit, 99.5–99.95% = 5% credit, 99.0–99.5% = 10% credit, <99.0% = 25% credit (applied to monthly service fee). We can adjust these bands per negotiation.

- Evidence & telemetry: I included a short evidence matrix in the SOW attachment — metrics we will export: per-region availability, p95/p99 latencies for common models, request routing maps, and the retention window (90 days by default, longer retention on request for enterprise accounts).

- On-call and failover: the SOW attachment lists the on-call escalation path and an expected RTO for regional failover (target 30 minutes for automatic routing failover, human-in-the-loop failover within 2 hours for complex evictions).

Next steps: Karthik will review the telemetry items for completeness; David is on the hook to align the order-form line items with procurement-friendly wording (billing/credits). Once we all agree, I can upload a DocuSign-ready annex and an order-form snippet you can drop into your purchase order.

Can you confirm whether procurement needs a signed statement from a security reviewer (SOC2 evidence) to accept the carve-out? If so we’ll include a short attestation and evidence link.

I attached: redwood_sla_annex_draft_v1.pdf, SOW-reliability-exhibit.docx, telemetry-evidence-matrix.csv

Best,
Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0132
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia@pioneerlabs.com>
Cc: David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability annex request + SOW attachments for order form

Hi all — quick technical clarifications from infra/serving runtime perspective so the annex is implementable: 

1) Carve-out mechanics: We agree to the 48-hour scheduled-bulk notification. Implementation detail: requests must include HTTP header X-RDW-SCHEDULED-BULK: true and the expected start/end times. That flag enables different routing (burst cluster) and excludes those samples from SLA aggregation.

2) Telemetry package: The telemetry-evidence-matrix includes sample Grafana dashboards and a list of Prometheus metrics we’ll provide (request_success_total, request_latency_seconds_bucket, regional_request_rate). We’ll provide CSV extracts for the three most-recent incidents on request as part of the evidence flow.

3) Latency tiers: For models heavier than 2B parameters or sequences >2048 tokens we’ll use a separate latency band (p95 <= 1.2s). We should call this out so expectations are correct across your model mix.

4) Maintenance windows & scheduled upgrades: we will surface monthly maintenance windows in the console and provide a 72-hour pre-notification for upgrades that may affect availability. Planned maintenance will not be counted against the SLA.

I flagged a couple of line edits in the annex (see redline comments in the attached PDF). My ask of procurement/legal: include a sentence in the order form that references the annex by name and version (e.g., "Redwood Reliability Annex v1 — RDW-20071-Pioneer"). That makes DocuSign routing and future amendment easier.

Soojin — can you confirm the evidence retention policy is 90 days by default and note options for extended retention?

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Olivia Grant <olivia@pioneerlabs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Torres <mtorres@pioneerlabs.com>, procure@pioneerlabs.com
Date: Sun, 25 Jun 2028 22:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reliability annex request + SOW attachments for order form

Kimberly — this is great, thanks to you and the team. A few quick confirmations from procurement/legal side after an initial pass: 

- The credit schedule looks reasonable; legal would like the ability to scale the bands if we exceed a $500k ARR threshold in the future — can we add a clause that allows mutually agreeable re-banding for large volume customers?

- The scheduled-bulk carve-out with the X-RDW-SCHEDULED-BULK header is acceptable. Procurement asked that the order form require the customer to notify Redwood’s procurement alias (procure@pioneerlabs.com) and include the scheduled start/end times in the DocuSign order metadata.

- SOC2 attestation: Pioneer requires a short statement that Redwood has SOC2 Type II controls in place for the production tier referenced in the annex. If you can provide a one-paragraph attestation and link to the SOC2 report (redacted) that would accelerate legal review.

If you can incorporate the small edit to allow re-banding at high ARR and add the SOC2 attestation paragraph to the annex, we can route this through DocuSign next Tuesday (Jun 28). Please send the DocuSign-ready annex + order-form snippet when you’re ready.

Thanks again — Olivia

--
Olivia Grant
Head of Platform Engineering | Pioneer Labs
